drafted_from: tool row in tools/start-a-computer/tool-rows.json, do-work/start-a-computer.mjs (placeStatus) and tools/start-a-computer/test/start-a-computer.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Is my computer arm1 running, and does its sign-up page at place.example.com answer?"
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads a lease file and asks the provider and the public sign-up page.
instructions: 1. Have the lease file a start or rent wrote (lease.json).

2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:read-a-computer"} and runs node tools/start-a-computer/do-work/start-a-computer.mjs status lease.json (the provider credential on descriptor 3 for a rented machine, none for one you run).
3. Read the JSON line: name, provider, lease_state, machine {state, address}, host_name and sign_up_status (200 means the public /readyz page answers).

worked_examples.title: A machine the person runs, asked once at its public name
worked_examples.ask: Is my computer up and answering?
worked_examples.given: Read from do-work/start-a-computer.mjs (placeStatus) with the lease from tools/start-a-computer/test/start-a-computer.test.mjs (first test) plus "state":"running": lease.json = {"schema":"place-lease/1","provider":"existing-machine","name":"arm1","state":"running","address":"192.0.2.9","adopted":true,"hostName":"place.example.com"}; https://place.example.com/readyz answers 200. Run: node tools/start-a-computer/do-work/start-a-computer.mjs status lease.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"name":"arm1","provider":"existing-machine","lease_state":"running","machine":{"state":"running","address":"192.0.2.9"},"host_name":"place.example.com","sign_up_status":200}: for an adopted machine the state is the lease's own, no provider is asked, and the page is asked once.
